title: CredLeakBench: Evaluating Credential Leakage and Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.08871v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly deployed to automate everyday digital chores from managing emails and social media to handling banking and bills allowing users to step away from supervision. However, this capability also exposes sensitive information to phishing. Safe execution requires distinguishing malicious requests from genuine ones without simply refusing to act. Despite its practical importance, this problem remains underexplored and it is unclear whether current agents or existing defenses can achieve it. To study this problem, we first propose CredLeak-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate how effectively and securely agents automate human workflows when confronted with phishing and identity verification. translated_title: CredLeakBench：评估大语言模型智能体中的凭据泄露与恢复
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体正被越来越多地部署用来自动化日常数字事务——从管理电子邮件和社交媒体到处理银行业务和账单支付——从而使用户可以脱离监督。然而，这种能力也使敏感信息暴露于网络钓鱼攻击之下。安全的执行要求智能体能够区分恶意请求与真实请求，而不是简单地拒绝执行。尽管这一问题具有重要的实际意义，但目前仍未得到充分研究，且尚不清楚当前的智能体或现有防御措施能否实现这一点。为了研究这一问题，我们首先提出了 CredLeakBench，这是一个综合性基准，旨在评估智能体在面临网络钓鱼和身份验证场景时自动化人类工作流程的有效性与安全性。该基准涵盖用户明确指示的身份验证以及自主收件箱监控两种场景，在后一种场景中，智能体并未被明确指示进行登录。该基准系统地变化欺骗性线索，并配对……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了 CredLeakBench 基准，用于评估大语言模型智能体在面对网络钓鱼与身份验证场景时区分恶意请求与真实请求、防止凭据泄露并安全自动化用户工作流程的能力。
en_tdlr: We propose CredLeakBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating how effectively and securely LLM agents distinguish phishing from genuine requests and prevent credential leakage when automating user workflows such as authentication and inbox monitoring.
